Subject: Tenant geofence & retention — verification runbook and evidence

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the call last week. As we move toward signing the Dedicated/VPC agreement, Medicore's Security & Compliance team has a short list of evidence requests we need clarified for our internal auditors and legal: 

- Exact deletion semantics for tenant-owned data in a private VPC (what you call "customer-controlled storage"). We need the operational steps and artefacts that prove delete.
- How snapshots/backups are handled (are we guaranteed no replica outside the geofenced region?) and expected retention windows for those artifacts.
- KMS/HSM model: can keys remain in our KMS? If Redwood holds keys, what's the rotation/attestation process?
- A sample "handback" runbook that lists the sequence of operations Redwood will perform (and artifacts produced) during a tenant offboarding + data-handback request.

Can you send a concise runbook and list of evidence items (signed attestation, snapshot IDs, audit log ranges, etc.)? We need to present that to our CISO and legal by EOW (Fri).

Appreciate it — Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Cloud Security | Medicore Health
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below, and attached is a draft runbook we typically provide for Private/VPC customers (handback_runbook_v2.pdf). Short summary: 

1) Customer-controlled storage and proof-of-delete
- For Private deployments where the customer opts to host data in their VPC-backed object store (S3/GCS equivalent), Redwood operates the inference runtime but does not persist tenant payloads in our shared storage. Persistent artifacts either remain in the customer bucket or are written to a customer-managed block/volume that is explicitly under your tenancy.
- Delete semantics: when a delete request is triggered (customer-led or contract termination), the runbook invokes a deterministic sequence: stop ingestion pipelines, disable new writes, snapshot final state (snapshot IDs recorded), trigger object-level deletes in the customer bucket, and then schedule a verification job that checks object manifests and object tombstones.
- Evidence we produce: list of deleted object keys, snapshot ID(s), KMS log entries for any envelope keys we touched, and a signed attestation PDF (we provide a DocuSign flow if you want signature capture).

2) Snapshots and replication
- By default we do not replicate tenant blob data to other regions if you select "region-locked" deployment at onboarding. Any optional replication is explicitly configured and documented in the onboarding SOW. Backups/snapshots for system-level metadata (not blobs) are kept in the same region unless you opt into cross-region DR.
- Retention: snapshots are retained per the SOW; typical retention is 30 days for ephemeral snapshots and 90 days for recovery snapshots unless the account requests otherwise. We can shorten retention on request and reflect in the SOW.

3) KMS/HSM
- Options: (A) Customer-managed KMS (recommended): Redwood uses your KMS for envelope keys; we never see plaintext. (B) Redwood-managed KMS with HSM attestations: we can hold keys but provide rotation logs and HSM-derived attestation artifacts. Both options listed in the attached matrix (kms_key_rotation_matrix.xlsx).

4) Runbook and SLAs
- Attached runbook includes step-by-step commands, roles (Redwood operator, customer operator), expected artifacts, and an evidence checklist. Typical offboarding window is 5 business days for standard handbacks; expedited handbacks (48–72 hours) are available under an addendum.

Next steps: I've attached the runbook and the KMS matrix. Jonas and Marissa are copied for any technical clarifications. If Medicore Legal wants a standard attestation template, we can generate one and send via DocuSign.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 9:05 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Delete semantics: when a delete request is triggered (customer-led or contract termination), the runbook invokes a deterministic sequence: stop ingestion pipelines, disable new writes, snapshot final state (snapshot IDs recorded), trigger object-level deletes in the customer bucket, and then schedule a verification job that checks object manifests and object tombstones.

Adding a couple of technical clarifications from the runtime/ops side: 
- Snapshot chain: snapshots are content-addressed and we publish the final snapshot manifest to your provided bucket (manifest contains the blob checksums and object keys). If you require, we will also publish an audit manifest to a read-only path that only Medicore can access.
- Tombstone verification: the verification job compares the final manifest to the live bucket listing and flags any missing tombstones. We also produce an "erase report" that enumerates object keys and a SHA256 of each deleted object as observed before deletion (where we had a cached copy). For objects we never cached (direct-streamed writes), the erase report contains the object key and the last-modified timestamp as proof of attempted deletion.
- Immutable backups: if you have an immutable backup policy in your bucket (e.g., object lock/retention), we coordinate a retention-lift request as part of the handback (requires Medicore operator approval). This is documented in the runbook.

I'll be available if you want a 30-min deep-dive on the manifest format and the erase-report schema.

— Jonas
